name: Close a window from script
plain: Closes windows the script opened; ordinary tabs cannot be closed by script.
meaning: A page can close a popup it created (for example after sign in), but it cannot kill the tab the person opened, which prevents sites from trapping or hiding.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Only script-closable windows; frames cannot close their parent
steps: If the window is script-closable, it closes
Otherwise console warns and nothing happens

limits.headline: Can close windows it opened itself, but not your regular tabs
limits.user_action: Nothing for its own windows. It happens when you finish a sign in or tap Done.
can: Close a popup or window that the page opened
Close a sign in window when it is finished
Close a window after a payment completes
cannot: Close a tab you opened yourself
Close a window it did not open
Close a tab with other history in it in most browsers

story.what_it_is: A page can close windows it opened, but not your ordinary tabs.
story.for_you: A small sign in or payment window closes itself when it is done. A normal page cannot shut your other tabs.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to tidy up their own pop ups after sign in or payment. The browser blocks the rest so sites cannot slam your tabs shut.

use_cases.example: A Sign in with Google window closes itself after you approve.
A PayPal pop up closes after you confirm, returning you to the shop.
A browser game portal closes its leaderboard pop up after you pick a player.
A phishing flow opens and closes windows quickly to hide a redirect.
A pop out chat window shuts itself when the stream ends.
A company tool closes its single sign on pop up when login is done.

technical_bounds: Script-closable only: opened by window.open, or the tab has a single session history entry (HTML spec)
Firefox adds dom.allow_scripts_to_close_windows (default false for non-script windows)
Chrome logs: Scripts may close only the windows that were opened by them
Cannot close the browser or other windows
